title: Kernel eval adjacent deltas - onboarding regression brief
content:
Summary:
This note captures the regression deltas we observed while onboarding model-2025-13 under three combined runtime/kernel changes: enabling FlashAttention-v2 kernels, switching Paged-KV cache page-size/thresholds (paged-kv config group B), and turning on continuous micro-batching (cont-batching warmup=25ms). The goal: surface functional regressions (generation quality), distributional shifts (logprobs / token-level deltas), and performance tradeoffs (p99 latency, median latency, throughput, token-cost).

Quick findings (high-level):
- Quality deltas: small but consistent increase in top-token sampling entropy for long-context prompts (>2k tokens) when paged-kv page-size reduced to 16KB. This appears as more frequent minor hallucinations on closed-book QA prompt sets (see examples).
- FlashAttention-v2: improved median generation latency by ~8–12% on A100 + mixed-precision paths, minimal quality impact when used alone. But combined with paged-kv aggressive paging it exposed a timing window that increased KV cache misses during cont-batching transitions.
- Continuous batching: improved throughput by 18% for small requests (<128 tokens) but introduced a tail-latency bump (~+22% p99) on spike traffic due to batching coagulation at burst boundaries.
- Composite effect: the worst regressions (quality + latency) show up only when all three features are enabled. Individually the changes are acceptable.

Background / motivation:
We onboarded model-2025-13 as a candidate for Hosted-API mid-tier. Perf goal: median gen latency < 80ms for 256-token responses at scale; cost target: tokens-per-second improved by 20% versus baseline runtime. Recent kernel updates (FA v2) and storage/kv paging improvements promised better memory efficiency and throughput; cont-batching is a runtime change aimed at smoothing tail cost. We ran a targeted regression sweep to validate these claims vs baseline runtime (FA v1, paged-kv default, cont-batching off).

Test matrix and config keys (condensed):
- Baseline: flash-attn=v1, paged-kv=default(page_size=32KB, threshold=0.65), cont-batching=off
- Variant A: flash-attn=v2, paged-kv=default, cont-batching=off
- Variant B: flash-attn=v1, paged-kv=aggressive(page_size=16KB, threshold=0.45), cont-batching=off
- Variant C: flash-attn=v1, paged-kv=default, cont-batching=on(warmup=25ms, max_batch=64)
- Variant D (prod candidate): flash-attn=v2, paged-kv=aggressive, cont-batching=on (all three)
- Canary sampling scheme: 5k requests per variant across distributed pods, split across 3 workload buckets (short chit-chat, code-completion, long-context closed-book QA).

Prompt sets used (representative names):
- short-chat-lite: 2–6 token prompts, stochastic generation tests
- code-snippets-small: code completion seeds with unit-test style prompts
- long-ctx-closedbook-2k: multi-paragraph questions requiring recall beyond 1k tokens
- rate-limited-burst: synthetic burst traffic to evaluate tail behavior
- halluc-test-50: 50 curated queries known to amplify hallucinations on earlier kernels

Metrics captured (per-request):
- latency_ms: median, p95, p99
- throughput: tokens/sec observed per worker
- correctness: exact-match (where applicable), ROUGE-L / BLEU for summarization-like prompts
- token-logprob-delta: average difference in logprob for top-5 tokens vs baseline
- entropy-topk: distributional uncertainty measure (top-5 Shannon entropy)
- kv-miss-events: internal metric counting page-loads / misses
- cost-estimate: per-request estimated GPU-token cost (normalized)

Results highlights (detailed):
1) Variant A (FlashAttention-v2 alone):
   - median latency: -10% vs baseline (good)
   - p99 latency: -4% (small improvement)
   - quality: negligible delta across short-chat and code snippets (EM and BLEU within ±0.3%)
   - long-ctx-closedbook: tiny increase in token-level entropy (+0.02 bits avg), not significant alone.
   - notes: FA v2 performs best under FP16 kernels on Tesla/A100-like stacks; no observable KV side-effects when paged-kv default is used.

2) Variant B (Paged-KV aggressive alone):
   - memory footprint: -12% (good for packing more models per GPU)
   - median latency: +3% (slight regression), p99: +9%
   - surface quality differences on long-context prompts: increased incorrect entity recall in ~7/500 queries; EM drop of 1.2 pts on that promptset
   - internal: kv-miss-events increased by 3.8x vs baseline for sequences >1k tokens because of more frequent page evictions.
   - hypothesis: reduced page size increases number of page boundaries, elevating page-load overhead at high context lengths.

3) Variant C (Continuous batching alone):
   - throughput: +18% for small requests (<128 tokens)
   - median latency: -6%
   - p99: +22% on synthetic bursts (rate-limited-burst promptset) due to coagulation and delayed flush
   - quality: no measurable quality shift
   - mitigation idea: lower max_wait for cont-batching on infra tier with bursty traffic; add fast-path for priority requests.

4) Variant D (All three enabled): composite observations:
   - median latency: -6% (net positive)
   - p99 latency: +28% (worse than any single variant)
   - quality: EM drop of 2.1 pts on long-ctx-closedbook, hallucination incidence up from 1.4% -> 4.9% on halluc-test-50
   - token-logprob-delta: mean top-token logprob reduced by ~0.17 (more uncertain), concentrated on token positions directly after page reload boundaries
   - kv-miss-events: highest (up 6.2x); cont-batching created compact bursts of requests that aligned poorly with page refill timing, FA-v2 kernel scheduling introduced micro-timing differences that exposed race conditions in KV cache warmup path.

Representative failure snippets (from long-ctx-closedbook):
- Prompt: "List the four inventions P. D. S. is credited with in his 1985 paper and which institutions funded them."
  - Baseline: correctly lists 4 items with institution attributions.
  - Variant D: lists 3 items, inventors swapped for one item, adds an invented funding source (hallucination).
  - Trace: sharp drop in top-token logprob at token 42 (start of institution attribution), coincident with kv-page-load event timestamp.

Root-cause hypotheses (priority-ordered):
1) Timing interaction between cont-batching flush/warmup and paged-kv async page-loads: when cont-batching aggregates multiple small requests, their combined reference pattern causes concurrent page boundary hits leading to serialized page-load stalls that inflate tail latency and perturb logits.
2) FA-v2 scheduling reorders kernel launch timings slightly relative to v1 (better median throughput) but that reordering means KV warmup and attention kernel execution overlap differently, exposing race windows that were previously masked.
3) Page-size reduction increases the frequency of page swaps; combined with hypothesis (1) this both increases overhead and increases the probability samples see abrupt contexts with incomplete KV state leading to logprob discontinuities.

Action items (short-term):
- [P0] Reproduce Variant D failures deterministically in lab with a controlled synthetic workload that reproduces page-boundary alignment; create a minimal reprod harness (Diego). Target: reproducible within 24 hours.
- [P0] Add guard: when cont-batching is on, delay batch flush if outstanding async page-loads > N (temporary mitigation; Marco).
- [P1] Run FA-v2 microbench with explicit serialization points to check for kernel launch reordering (Janet).
- [P1] Re-evaluate paged-kv page_size=24KB intermediate config to trade memory vs page-load frequency (Priya).
- [P2] Add a per-token continuity health metric in eval harness that flags abrupt logprob dips aligned with kv-miss-events (Aisha).

Longer-term recommendations:
- Implement page-prefetch heuristics driven by cont-batching patterns: if a batch contains requests with long-context tokens that cluster around same key-positions, prefetch neighbor pages asynchronously before flush.
- Consider adapting the cont-batching coagulation threshold for high-variability traffic tiers (e.g., reduce warmup or provide opt-out header for low-latency customers).
- Add kernel-level instrumentation for attention start/end timestamps, and correlate with KV page lifecycle events to produce traceable sequences for root cause analysis.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the FA-v2 timing sensitivity reproducible across GPU families (H100 vs A100)? We tested only A100 so far.
- How much of the hallucination pattern is model-specific vs kernel/paging? Need a second model (model-2024-81) sweep.
- Does increasing page_size to 48KB remove quality regression while still meeting memory density targets? trade study required.

Appendix A — sample harness commands (lab):
- run_sweep --model model-2025-13 --variants A,B,C,D --samples 5000 --promptset long-ctx-closedbook-2k --trace-kv --dump-logprobs
- reproduce_burst --promptset rate-limited-burst --cont-batching on --warmup 25 --duration 30m --trace p99

Appendix B — quick raw numbers (median across 5 runs):
- Baseline: median=94ms, p99=340ms, throughput=1.0x, EM(long-ctx)=72.4
- Variant A: median=84ms, p99=326ms, throughput=1.04x, EM=72.2
- Variant B: median=97ms, p99=370ms, throughput=1.01x, EM=71.2
- Variant C: median=88ms, p99=415ms, throughput=1.18x, EM=72.3
- Variant D: median=88ms, p99=435ms, throughput=1.16x, EM=70.3

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is a working brief — we prioritized finding reproducible failure modes over exhaustive parameter sweeps. Please add findings to the linked confluence page and tag any infra/serving owners.
- Questions: should we roll back FA-v2 in the canary until mitigations land, or patch cont-batching guard first? My inclination: block combined rollout (Variant D) for Hosted mid-tier until we have page-prefetch or cont-batching guard.

References / links: see linked_artifacts for PRs and Jira.

End of brief.
